Joseph H. Lewis
Film director (1907-2000)Joseph H. Lewis was an American director and editor of film and television. In a 30-year directorial career, he directed numerous low-budget westerns, action pictures, musicals, adventures, and thrillers. His stylish B-movies came to be appreciated by auteur theory-espousing film critics in the years following his retirement in 1966. Today he is remembered for mysteries and films noir: My Name Is Julia Ross and So Dark the Night as well as his most highly regarded features, 1950's Gun Crazy, which spotlighted a desperate young couple who embark on a deadly crime spree, and The Big Combo, with its critically acclaimed cinematography by John Alton.
